correctness.rationale: In affine coordinates over the two edges the area measure becomes uniform on the unit square. The side tests are k<x+ky<1 and ell<y+ell x<1 when testing both parallel feet, with each endpoint inequality separately testing one foot. For generic interior points, a corner is a normal base exactly when it is a strict local maximum of squared distance on the boundary: the vector to the point has positive dot products with both outgoing edges. There are no vertex minima, since the vector to the point is a positive combination of the outgoing edges and has positive squared length. Side interiors contribute only minima, so there are equally many feet and corner bases, with at least two of each from the two automatic opposite corner maxima. In the eight-normal event the four tests give a rectangle in the transformed (x+ky,y+ell x) plane. Its inverse corners lie in the unit square for ell<1 and its Jacobian is 1-k ell; the rectangle is empty when ell>=1. Separately the per-foot area is 1-z/2 for z<=1 and 1/(2z) for z>=1, at z=k or ell. This gives the claimed mean and, together with the eight-normal area, solves the three probabilities. At ell=1 the common probabilities are (c^2,1-c^2,0); c=0 gives (0,0,1). For fixed c>0, q+1/q strictly increases from q=1; in the first regime p4 and p8 decrease and p6 increases, whereas beyond the threshold p6 is proportional to 1/q and p4 increases. The mean is continuous and strictly decreases to 4. These checks establish the law and extrema without relying on the finite checker.
residual_risks: No statement is made about the excluded finitely many transition segments or degenerate parallelograms.

value.rationale: For a fundamental centrally symmetric polygon family this determines the entire random normal-count statistic, not merely its mean or maximal possible value. The aspect threshold separates positive-area and impossible eight-normal regimes, and the six-normal mode is maximized there rather than at the mean-maximizing rhombus. These structural and quantitative facts give a useful benchmark for chamber/active-region descriptions on more general polygons.
residual_risks: The value is specific to parallelograms and area sampling; the result does not classify general quadrilaterals.
